nodes.name: Bi-warped product
nodes.statement: Let $B,N_{1}$ and $N_{2}$ be Riemannian manifolds equipped with metrics $g_B,g_1$ and $g_{2}$, respectively, and let $f_{1},f_{2}$ be two positive functions on $B$. Then the {\it bi-warped product} $B\times_{f_{1}} N_{1}\times_{f_{2}} N_{2}$ is the product manifold $B\times N_{1}\times N_{2}$ equipped with the bi-warped product metric \begin{equation} g=g_B+f_{1}^2 g_1+f_{2}^2 g_2.\end{equation}
differentia: equipped with the bi-warped product metric
nodes.statement_short: $B\times_{f_1}N_1\times_{f_2}N_2$ is $B\times N_1\times N_2$ with metric $g_B+f_1^2g_1+f_2^2g_2$ for positive warping functions on $B$.

nodes.name: CR submanifold
nodes.statement: A submanifold $M$ of a Kaehler manifold $(\widetilde M, \widetilde g,J)$ is called a {\it $CR$ submanifold} \cite{bejancu} if there exist a holomorphic distribution $\mathfrak D^{T}$ and a totally real distribution $\mathfrak D^\perp$ on $M$ such that $TM=\mathfrak D^{T}\oplus \mathfrak D^\perp$, where $TM$ denotes the tangent bundle of $M$.
differentia: there exist a holomorphic distribution $\mathfrak D^{T}$ and a totally real distribution $\mathfrak D^\perp$ on $M$ such that $TM=\mathfrak D^{T}\oplus \mathfrak D^\perp$

nodes.name: Non-existence of warped products N_perp x_f N_T in Kaehler manifolds
nodes.statement: In particular, he proved in \cite{C3} that there do not exist warped products of the form $N_{\perp}\times_{f} N_{T}$ in any Kaehler manifold, where $N_{T}$ is a holomorphic submanifold and $N_{\perp}$ is a totally real submanifold.
assumptions: $N_{T}$ is a holomorphic submanifold and $N_{\perp}$ is a totally real submanifold
conclusions: there do not exist warped products of the form $N_{\perp}\times_{f} N_{T}$ in any Kaehler manifold

nodes.name: Chen's inequality for CR-warped products
nodes.statement: On the other hand, he proved that, for any warped product of the form $M=N_{T}\times_f N^{n_{1}}_{\perp}$ in any Kaehler manifold, the second fundamental form $h$ of $M$ satisfies $$||h||^2\geq 2n_1 ||\nabla(\ln f)||^2,$$ where $n_{1}=\dim\,N^{n_{1}}_{\perp}$ and $\nabla (\ln f)$ is the gradient of $\ln f$.
assumptions: for any  warped product of the form $M=N_{T}\times_f N^{n_{1}}_{\perp}$ in any Kaehler manifold
conclusions: the second fundamental form $h$ of $M$ satisfies $$||h||^2\geq 2n_1 ||\nabla(\ln f)||^2,$$
nodes.statement_short: For a warped product $N_T\times_f N_\perp$ in a Kaehler manifold, $\|h\|^2\ge 2n_1\|\nabla\ln f\|^2$.

nodes.name: CR-warped product
nodes.statement: He simply called such warped product submanifolds $N_{T}\times_f N^{n_{1}}_{\perp}$ to be {\it $CR$-warped products}.

nodes.name: Contact metric manifold
nodes.statement: A $(2m+1)$-dimensional Riemannian manifold $(\widetilde M^{2m+1}, g)$ is said to be a {\it{contact metric manifold}} if it admits a $(1, 1)$ tensor field $\varphi$ on its tangent bundle $T\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, a vector field ${\mathfrak{\xi}}$ (i.e., the structure vector field) and a $1$-form $\eta$ satisfying: \begin{equation}\begin{aligned} &\varphi^2=-Id+\eta\otimes{\mathfrak{\xi}},\,\,\,\eta({\mathfrak{\xi}})=1,\,\,\,\varphi(\xi)=0,\,\,\,\eta\circ\varphi=0,\\ &g(\varphi X, \varphi Y)=g(X, Y)-\eta(X)\eta(Y),\,\,\,\eta(X)=g(X, {\mathfrak{\xi}}). \end{aligned}\end{equation} for any vector fields $X, Y$ on $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, where $\widetilde\nabla$ denotes the Riemannian connection with respect to the Riemannian metric $g$ (see \cite{Bl}).
differentia: it admits a $(1, 1)$ tensor field $\varphi$ on its tangent bundle $T\widetilde M^{2m+1}$, a vector field ${\mathfrak{\xi}}$ (i.e., the structure  vector field) and a $1$-form $\eta$ satisfying:
nodes.statement_short: A $(2m+1)$-dim Riemannian manifold with $(\varphi,\xi,\eta)$ satisfying the almost contact metric relations (2.1).

nodes.name: Almost contact metric structure relations
nodes.statement: \begin{aligned} &\varphi^2=-Id+\eta\otimes{\mathfrak{\xi}},\,\,\,\eta({\mathfrak{\xi}})=1,\,\,\,\varphi(\xi)=0,\,\,\,\eta\circ\varphi=0,\\ &g(\varphi X, \varphi Y)=g(X, Y)-\eta(X)\eta(Y),\,\,\,\eta(X)=g(X, {\mathfrak{\xi}}). \end{aligned}
nodes.label: struc

nodes.name: Normal almost contact metric manifold
nodes.statement: An almost contact metric manifold $(\widetilde M, g, \varphi, \xi, \eta)$ is said to be {\textit{normal}} if the tensor field $N_{\varphi}=[\varphi, \varphi]+2d\eta\otimes\xi$ vanishes identically, where $[\varphi, \varphi]$ denotes the Nijenhuis tensor of $\varphi$.

nodes.name: Sasakian manifold
nodes.statement: A normal contact metric manifold is said to be a {\textit{Sasakian manifold}}.

nodes.name: Characterization of Sasakian manifolds
nodes.statement: An almost contact metric manifold is Sasakian if and only if \begin{align} (\widetilde\nabla_X\varphi)Y=g(X, Y){\mathfrak{\xi}}-\eta(Y)X,\,\,\,\widetilde\nabla_X{\mathfrak{\xi}}=-\varphi X, \end{align} for any $X, Y\in\Gamma(T\widetilde M)$, where $\Gamma(T\widetilde M)$ is the Lie algebra of vector fields on $\widetilde M$.
assumptions: for any $X, Y\in\Gamma(T\widetilde M)$
conclusions: An almost contact metric manifold is Sasakian if and only if
nodes.statement_short: An almost contact metric manifold is Sasakian iff $(\widetilde\nabla_X\varphi)Y=g(X,Y)\xi-\eta(Y)X$ and $\widetilde\nabla_X\xi=-\varphi X$.

nodes.name: Sasakian structure equations
nodes.statement: (\widetilde\nabla_X\varphi)Y=g(X, Y){\mathfrak{\xi}}-\eta(Y)X,\,\,\,\widetilde\nabla_X{\mathfrak{\xi}}=-\varphi X,
nodes.label: sasaki

nodes.name: Almost cosymplectic manifold
nodes.statement: An almost contact metric manifold is called {\em{almost cosymplectic}} if $d\eta=0$ and $d\varphi=0$ according to D. E. Blair in \cite{Bl}.

nodes.name: Cosymplectic manifold
nodes.statement: In particular, an almost cosymplectic manifold is called {\em{cosymplectic}} if it satisfies \begin{align} \widetilde\nabla\varphi=0,\quad \widetilde\nabla\xi=0. \end{align}

nodes.name: Cosymplectic condition
nodes.statement: \widetilde\nabla\varphi=0,\quad \widetilde\nabla\xi=0.
nodes.label: cosy

nodes.name: Mean curvature vector
nodes.statement: The mean curvature vector $H$ is defined by $H=\frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} h(e_i, e_i)$.

nodes.name: Totally geodesic, totally umbilical and minimal submanifolds
nodes.statement: A submanifold $M$ is called {\it totally geodesic} if $h=0$; {\it totally umbilical} if $h(X, Y)=g(X, Y)H$; and {\it minimal} if $H=0$.

nodes.name: Invariant submanifold
nodes.statement: (a) A submanifold $M^{2n+1}$ tangent to ${\mathfrak{\xi}}$ is called {\textit{invariant}} if $\varphi$ preserves each tangent space of $M^{2n+1}$, i.e., $\varphi(T_xM^{2n+1})\subseteq T_xM^{2n+1}, \forall x\in M^{2n+1}$.

nodes.name: Anti-invariant submanifold
nodes.statement: (b) A submanifold $M^{n}$ is called {\textit{anti-invariant}} if $\varphi$ maps any tangent space of $M^{n}$ into the corresponding normal space, i.e., $\varphi(T_xM^{n})\subset T^\perp_xM^{n}, \forall x\in M^{n}$.
differentia: $\varphi$ maps any tangent space of $M^{n}$ into the corresponding normal space

nodes.name: Pointwise slant submanifold
nodes.statement: (c) A submanifold $M^{n}$ is called {\textit{pointwise slant}} \cite{Etayo,CG} if for any nonzero vector $X\in T_xM^n\,(x\in M)$, the angle $\theta(X)$ between $\varphi X$ and $T_xM^n$ is independent of the choice of $X\in T_xM$.
differentia: the angle $\theta(X)$ between $\varphi X$ and $T_xM^n$ is independent of the choice of $X\in T_xM$

nodes.name: Slant function
nodes.statement: In this case, $\theta$ defines a function on $M^n$, called the {\textit{slant function}}.

nodes.name: Slant submanifold
nodes.statement: In particular, if the slant function $\theta$ is a global constant on $M^{n}$, then $M^{n}$ is said to be a {\it slant submanifold} or a {\it $\theta$-slant submanifold}.
differentia: the slant function $\theta$ is a global constant on $M^{n}$

nodes.name: Anti-invariant submanifolds are slant with angle pi/2
nodes.statement: Anti-invariant submanifolds are slant submanifolds with slant function $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$.
conclusions: Anti-invariant submanifolds are slant submanifolds with slant function $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$.

nodes.name: Proper pointwise slant submanifold
nodes.statement: A pointwise slant submanifold is called {\it proper} if $0<\theta <\frac{\pi}{2}$.

nodes.name: Tangential and normal components T, F, t, f
nodes.statement: For any $X\in\Gamma(TM^n)$ and $N\in \Gamma(T^{\perp}M^n)$, we put $$\varphi X = T X + FX,\quad \varphi N = tN+fN,$$ where $TX$ (resp., $tN$) is the tangential component, and $FX$ (resp., $fN$) is the normal component of $\varphi X$ (resp. of $\varphi N$).
nodes.statement_short: Split $\varphi X=TX+FX$ and $\varphi N=tN+fN$ into tangential and normal components.

nodes.name: Characterization of pointwise slant submanifolds
nodes.statement: Let $M^n$ be a submanifold of an almost contact metric manifold $\widetilde M^{2m+1}$ with $\mathfrak{\xi}\in\Gamma(TM^n)$. conclusions: Then $M^n$ is pointwise slant if and only if

nodes.statement: From \eqref{sasaki} and \eqref{gauss}, we have \begin{align} A_\mathfrak{\xi}X=TX,\quad \nabla^\perp_X\xi=-FX, \end{align} for any $X\in\Gamma(TM)$. Taking the inner product in \eqref{cs1} with $Y\in\Gamma(TM)$, we get \begin{align} g(h(X, Y), \mathfrak{\xi})=g(TX, Y). \end{align} From \eqref{cs2}, we find $\cos^2\theta\;g(X, Y)=0$ via polarization identity. Since, the metric $g$ is Riemannian, we obtain $\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}$. The converse is trivial.
